overview: A Death Guard officer must carry a warning across a galaxy where even the journey home can no longer be taken for granted.
synopsis: Nathaniel Garro, a captain of the Death Guard, discovers that obedience to his Legion’s commanders and loyalty to the Emperor have become incompatible. With the help of warriors and civilians aboard the Eisenstein, he attempts to carry news of Isstvan to Terra.

The escape forces Garro to confront pursuit, a damaged ship and the dangers of the warp. Euphrati Keeler and her companions bring their own experience of the betrayal. Even reaching Imperial forces does not guarantee that the warning will be believed.
detailed: The story follows Garro’s service within the Death Guard and the tensions between his traditional sense of duty and the attitudes of some of his brothers. His relationships with his servant Kaleb and the warriors under his command establish the responsibilities he feels beyond simple obedience.

At Isstvan III, Garro receives the warning of betrayal and becomes part of the effort to preserve witnesses. The Eisenstein carries a small group that includes Keeler, Sindermann and Mersadie Oliton. Escaping the fleet requires decisions that make return to the old order impossible.

The vessel’s flight is threatened by hostile pursuit and the condition of its machinery. In the warp, corruption reaches the crew and warriors, including the transformation of Solun Decius. Garro and his companions must fight to keep the ship and its testimony intact.

After the Eisenstein becomes stranded, a desperate attempt to signal for rescue brings the survivors into contact with Rogal Dorn’s Imperial Fists. Dorn’s initial response is anger and disbelief: accepting their account means accepting that his brothers have turned against the Emperor.

The survivors are taken toward Terra, where their warning can enter the Imperium’s highest councils. Garro’s journey ends with his former certainty replaced by a new duty. His service will have to be defined by the truth of what he witnessed rather than by his Legion’s orders.
